issue: Two separately published Rubank volumes (Preparing for Kreutzer Vol. 1, Hal Leonard 0109 116; Vol. 2, 0109 216) are merged in one row, against the one-entry-per-volume rule. Vol. 1 holds four sections (first-position, higher-position, trill and double-stop etudes by Kayser, Dont, Mazas etc.); Vol. 2 has minor keys, bowing studies, advanced double stops and concert caprices. Level 3 looks right for Vol. 2 and a little high for Vol. 1 (Eastman CMS Levels 2-3, Shar ASTA grade 3).
suggested_title: Preparing for Kreutzer, Vol. 1 (and a separate row for Vol. 2)

issue: Two separately published Rubank volumes (Introducing the Positions Vol. 1, 3rd and 5th positions, Hal Leonard 0108 116; Vol. 2, 2nd, 4th, 6th and 7th positions, 0108 216) are merged in one row. The notes field is correct. Vol. 2 is the harder volume (Eastman CMS lists both volumes at Level 3 of 6).
suggested_title: Introducing the Positions, Vol. 1 (and a separate row for Vol. 2)

issue: Level too low. Title omits the descriptor that its companion Op. 63 carries: Op. 64 is the set of six études for left-hand technique (Wikipedia work list; the Hamelle edition issued Opp. 63 and 64 as Cahiers 1 and 2, plate J. 4324 H). Published in two parts (Part 1: The Left Hand; Part 2: The Bow). Under the one-entry-per-part rule it could be split; the single entry and Level 8 are otherwise fine.
suggested_title: The Artist's Technique of Violin Playing, Op. 12 Part 1 (The Left Hand) and Part 2 (The Bow)

issue: Category: a single posthumous étude (1886, first published 1989); IMSLP files it under Studies, so 'Études & Caprices' fits better than 'Solo Violin'.

Not wrong, but incomplete/vague. (1) notes 'Advanced classical études; high positions' misses the point: the set is mainly bowing-oriented (varied slurred/detached bowings, spiccato, chords) plus double stops, trills, extensions and shifts up to 9th position; suggest 'Bowing-led études: varied bowings, double stops, trills, shifts' (<=100 chars). (2) exams omits RCM Level 10, where the 2021 syllabus lists 'Gaviniès 24 études (Matinées) PET; INT: any one'; 'AMEB CertPerf (mvt)' and 'ASTA CAP 10' could not be verified here (ameb.edu.au refused automated access; the ASTACAP handbook is members-only). (3) set is empty: use set '24 Matinées' so the 24 new per-study rows group with it. (4) Level 8 is fine for the whole book (individual studies range 6-8). Retailers (e.g. Shar) claim the set covers all 24 keys; the scores use only 16 keys.

Published title is 'The School of Violin-Technics' (IMSLP: 'School of Violin Technics'), three books: Book 1 dexterity in the positions, Book 2 double stops, Book 3 bowing (G. Schirmer 1899-1900). The catalogue says 'Technique' and has no set, so Books 2-3 cannot be grouped. (RCM 2021's resource list does cite 'School of Violin Technique, 4 vols., Schirmer 2011', so the catalogue wording has a modern precedent; Schirmer's later 4-volume edition adds the Scale Studies.) Level 1 kept as the catalogue anchor.
suggested_title: School of Violin Technics, Book 1 (dexterity in the positions)

issue: Level 5 looks too high. Italian conservatory syllabi use Polo's 30 double-stop studies far earlier: Vibo Valentia CB54 sets 'the first ones' for the year-1 exam and the set for the final exam of the basic course (positions up to the 5th), next to Kayser Op. 20, Mazas Op. 36, Dont Op. 37, Sitt Op. 32; Cuneo (2017) places it in pre-academic period B1-B2 with Kayser and Sitt; the row's own exam list (RCM 6-8) also points to L2-L4. Title is right (IMSLP: 30 Studi a corde doppie).

Note says 'also used by violists', but the caprices were written for the viola: IMSLP gives instrumentation 'viola (or violin) (read frontispiece)' and Italian Wikipedia lists '41 Capricci per l'alto-viola'. Title, opus and level are fine; suggested note: 'Written for viola (or violin); Classical-era caprices on bowing, shifting and double stops'.

Level possibly too high: the LSU dissertation (Iltcheva 2006) says the 12 Caprices were instructional in purpose and 'fairly simple' in style, with an international reputation as performance and pedagogical pieces; title and dates are correct (composed 1953, formerly Concert Etudes in Folk Style). Consider level 7 (not 8).

Title wording is wrong: Op. 1 has no 'Book 1'. It is one school in four parts (Bosworth 'Part', Schirmer 'Book', Bärenreiter 'Vol.'): 1 first position, 2 positions 2–7, 3 shifting, 4 double/triple/quadruple stops, left-hand pizzicato and harmonics. 'Book 1 Part 4' misreads as Book 1 of something. Also the set is empty, so the four parts cannot be grouped (use set 'School of Violin Technique, Op. 1'), and the notes omit chords and harmonics (suggest 'Double stops, chords, left-hand pizzicato and harmonics'). Level 7 is fine.
suggested_title: School of Violin Technique, Op. 1 Part 4 (double stops)
